deep.reconstruction:
The page holds no worked derivation. It is a set of research notes and programmatic remarks, separated by rules. This page is evidently from Hilbert's early Königsberg notebook, so roughly the late 1880s.

(1) 'Formel für π auf demselben Wege finden, mittels welcher vielleicht die Irrationalität von π gezeigt wer[den kann]. *den Raum. (x²+y²=m)'
- 'Auf demselben Wege' refers back to the previous page. There Hilbert proposed estimating the number of solutions of Diophantine inequalities (a1x1+...+anxn<A, xy<A, xyz<A) by comparing a volume with the number of unit cubes the region contains or meets.
- Applied to the circle x²+y²≤m, the method gives the following (my filling-in, standard Gauss/Dirichlet material). Let N(m) = #{(x,y)∈Z²: x²+y²≤m}. Then N(m) = πm + O(√m), so π = lim N(m)/m.
- Arithmetically, with r2(n) = #{x²+y²=n} = 4·Σ_{d|n} χ₋₄(d), one gets N(m) = 1 + 4·Σ_{d odd≤m} (−1)^((d−1)/2)·⌊m/d⌋. Dividing by m and letting m→∞ yields Leibniz's series π/4 = 1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − ...
- Hilbert's further hope is that such a lattice-point formula might also yield the irrationality of π. That was already proved by Lambert in 1761, and transcendence by Lindemann in 1882. He also seems to want the spatial analogue: '*den Raum', i.e. x²+y²+z²=m and the ball volume 4π/3.
- Nothing is carried out.

(2) 'Realitätsfragen: Kronecker, Klein, Dyck, Fr. Meyer.' This is a literature list on 'reality questions': the number and topology of real roots, real branches and real circuits of algebraic curves and surfaces. It covers Kronecker's characteristic/index theory for counting real roots, Klein's work on real curves, W. Dyck's analysis situs papers (1888) and Franz Meyer. This is the circle of ideas behind Hilbert's later 16th problem.

(3) 'Studiere: Schwarz über eine Minimumseigenschaft der Kugel und suche es abzukürzen.' This means H. A. Schwarz's proof (Göttinger Nachrichten 1884) that the sphere has least surface area among bodies of given volume. Hilbert intends to shorten that proof.
- He records a suggestion of Kronecker (referring to Kronecker's work on the volume of the tetrahedron): one should represent the volume of any body as '(ball) minus a definite form'. That is, write the isoperimetric deficit explicitly as a manifestly nonnegative (positive-definite) expression, so that the inequality S³ ≥ 36πV² follows at once with equality only for the sphere.

(4) 'Ueber ein fundamentales Axiom des menschlichen Verstandes. [added later, small:] Vielleicht dass jedes Problem lösbar ist?' This is the germ of the solvability axiom / 'no ignorabimus' of the 1900 Paris address and the 1930 Königsberg speech.

(5) 'Begriff der ganzen Zahl beruht nothwendig auf Zeit und Raum. Begriff der Stetigkeit einfacher als der Begriff der ganzen Zahl. Kant hat Recht.' This is a Kantian position: arithmetic rests on the forms of intuition, and continuity is conceptually prior to and simpler than the integer. It contrasts with the arithmetization of Dedekind, Kronecker and Weierstrass, and with Hilbert's own later views.

(6) 'In allen anderen Wissenschaften Material, von dem man nicht weiss, wo es herkommt ... Hier reines Denken, reine Philosophie. Kant hat das als der erste gefühlt, aber nicht bewiesen, er hat angefangen, aber nicht zu Ende geführt.' The claim is that mathematics, unlike the other sciences, is pure thought. Kant first sensed this but did not complete the argument.

Context: the next page continues the foundational theme with a Weierstrass quotation on the principles of mathematics.
errors: No computations are performed, so there are no computational errors.

The hope that a lattice-point formula for π might yield irrationality is speculative and was never realized; Lambert (1761) had already proved irrationality by continued fractions. The claim is not wrong as written, since it is phrased as 'vielleicht'.
'Begriff der Stetigkeit einfacher als als ...' contains a dittography ('als als') in the original.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'x den[?] Raum' is better read as '*den Raum'. The mark is an insertion/footnote asterisk with 'den' crossed or struck, presumably meaning '(für) den Raum', i.e. the spatial analogue.
Line 2: 'gezeigt wer.' is an abbreviation for 'gezeigt wer[den kann]'.
'nicht beweisen' should probably be read as 'nicht bewiesen'.
'den Inhalt jeden Körpers' – the image shows 'jeden Körper[s]' with a struck 'x' after it. This is consistent with the transcription; grammatically 'jedes'.

The insertion 'Vielleicht dass jedes Problem lösbar ist?' is written small, in a later-looking hand, above the end of the 'menschlichen Verstandes' line; the transcription's {+...+} marking is appropriate.
'Fr. Meyer' is correct (Franz Meyer), as is 'Dyck' (Walther Dyck).
